articles.excerpt: Every morning across engineering colleges and universities in India, hundreds of people line up in front of wall-mounted fingerprint machines that break down and cause morning delays. To solve this, w…
articles.body: Every morning across engineering colleges and universities in India, hundreds of people line up in front of wall-mounted fingerprint machines that break down and cause morning delays. To solve this, we built PrezScan ( https://prezscan.onrender.com ) — an independent, 100% free, hardware-free smart attendance web app engineered specifically for Indian higher-education campuses. Why PrezScan is Built for Colleges: Dual-Lock Anti-Proxy Attendance : Enforces a physical double-lock combining on-device 68-point AI facial recognition with academic building Wi-Fi subnet (CIDR) geofencing. Marking attendance outside the campus building or buddy-punching is physically impossible. Sub-200ms Verification : Runs client-side directly in the browser engine using WebGL GPU acceleration.

articles.title: Low-Cost Summarization Using OpenAI API Token Reduction in Node.js (and a Portable Choice)
articles.excerpt: Short answer: Low-cost summarization using the OpenAI API comes from reducing input tokens, capping output tokens, chunking long diffs, and keeping the Node.js or Go caller behind a provider-neutral c…
articles.body: Short answer: Low-cost summarization using the OpenAI API comes from reducing input tokens, capping output tokens, chunking long diffs, and keeping the Node.js or Go caller behind a provider-neutral contract; that combination lowers API cost without making one vendor the architecture. The practical answer is to reduce the text before it reaches the model, cap the output deliberately, and keep a provider-neutral summary contract around the call. For a logistics platform that turns code-review changes into structured findings, that usually means counting tokens, chunking oversized diffs, asking for a short JSON-shaped result, and retaining a fallback path when a provider rejects the context.

articles.title: Observability for AI Agents: Tracing, Evaluation and Cost Control in Production
articles.excerpt: How to understand, monitor, debug, and optimize agentic AI systems using OpenTelemetry and modern AI observability practices. Traditional backend observability is built around relatively predictable e…
articles.body: How to understand, monitor, debug, and optimize agentic AI systems using OpenTelemetry and modern AI observability practices. 1. Why Is Observability Different for AI Agents? Traditional backend observability is built around relatively predictable execution paths. A request enters an application, passes through several services, interacts with a database, and eventually returns a response. We can use logs, metrics, and distributed traces to understand what happened and where a problem occurred. AI agents introduce a different level of complexity. An agent does not necessarily follow a predefined execution path. It may call an LLM multiple times, select tools dynamically, retry failed operations, delegate tasks to other agents, retrieve external context, or wait for additional user input.

articles.title: Trimming Container Bloat with Docker History and Dive
articles.excerpt: Why this matters: Large container images increase pull times during CI/CD, consume unnecessary storage in container registries, and expand the attack surface by including extraneous binary dependencie…
articles.body: Why this matters: Large container images increase pull times during CI/CD, consume unnecessary storage in container registries, and expand the attack surface by including extraneous binary dependencies. Managing image size is a fundamental practice for maintaining lean, reproducible data pipelines that scale predictably across environments. A Docker image is not a single file; it is a stack of filesystem changes. A common misconception is that deleting a file in a later RUN command removes it from the final image. It does not. The file persists in the layer where it was created, and subsequent layers simply mark it as "hidden" or "deleted," meaning your image size remains bloated by the original data.

articles.title: James Webb Space Telescope uncovers new clues about the origins of 'interstellar invader' comet 3I/ATLAS
articles.excerpt: The findings are another clue towards understanding the origins of 3I/ATLAS and the planet-forming conditions around other stars.
articles.body: Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), scientists have found that the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS was built from tiny grains of ice mixed with dust that are quite different from the solar system’s comets. These ice grains do, however, bear striking similarities to some icy bodies located at the edge of the solar system, beyond the orbit of Neptune, so-called trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs). 3I/ATLAS was discovered entering the solar system in the summer of 2025. It was only the third object found entering the solar system from farther afield in the Milky Way after 1I/'Oumuamua , seen in 2017, and 2I/Borisov , detected in 2019. This meant the interstellar comet offered a rare chance to glimpse the conditions under which such bodies form in other star systems.

articles.title: Raising the quality of insights in agentic analytics
articles.excerpt: In just a few years, generative AI has changed the face of enterprise analytics, notably by making analytics accessible to users across the organization. Agentic AI promises to do even more, by automa…
articles.body: In just a few years, generative AI has changed the face of enterprise analytics, notably by making analytics accessible to users across the organization. Agentic AI promises to do even more, by automating entire workflows and taking actions based on agent insights. But there is a problem: The quality of insights that agents currently generate leaves much to be desired. Fewer than half of agent-generated insights at the organizations surveyed for this report lead to business improvement. And while most respondents praise the quality of their agents’ descriptive insights, reviews of their prescriptive insights—those on which actions are based—are decidedly mixed.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 2, 2000: Expedition 1 Arrives at the International Space Station
articles.excerpt: Expedition 1 crewmates Bill Shepherd, Yuri Gidzenko and Sergei Krikalev pose with a model of the space station as it appeared in 2000.
articles.body: On Nov. 2, 2000, the International Space Station welcomed its first long-term residents: NASA astronaut Bill Shepherd and two Russian cosmonauts, Yuri Gidzenko and Sergei Krikalev. The mission was called Expedition 1. Before this expedition, NASA had launched five, one-week-long Space Shuttle missions to help build the space station and bring up supplies. But this time, the crew would be staying for four and a half months, and they weren't taking the shuttle. Instead, they took a Russian Soyuz spacecraft , and this was the first Soyuz to ever dock at the space station. During their stay at the space station, they unpacked supplies and installed new equipment, including the first solar arrays.

articles.excerpt: In this image, we can see a colorful view of an ancient, rocky Martian hill.
articles.body: In this image, we can see a colorful view of an ancient, rocky Martian hill. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UArizona) This rainbow-hued rocky plain looks like the landscape of an alien world. And, it turns out, it is. What is it? In this image, we can see an ancient, rocky hill on Mars . In the Red Planet's Southern Highlands, this alien terrain is chock-full of minerals, which we can see clearly defined in this color-enhanced view of the region. This image was snapped by the HiRISE camera aboard NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter ( MRO ), which has been studying the planet's surface, atmosphere and climate since arriving in Martian orbit in March 2006. But this isn't exactly what the surface of the planet would look like through our eyes; the image is color-enhanced.

articles.title: Electric trucks hit 50% of China’s heavy truck sales, diesel demand falls
articles.excerpt: Electric trucks made up 50.3% of all heavy trucks sold in China in September. That’s 33,100 electric big rigs in a single month, up 37% from a year ago, while the overall heavy-truck market shrank by…
articles.body: Electric trucks made up 50.3% of all heavy trucks sold in China in September. That’s 33,100 electric big rigs in a single month, up 37% from a year ago, while the overall heavy-truck market shrank by 21%. And it’s showing up in the oil data. China’s diesel demand is on track to fall by about 230,000 barrels per day this year, and trucks running on batteries and natural gas are doing most of the work. more…

articles.title: Bestselling US e-bike Lectric XP4 relaunched in limited-edition with new colors and gear
articles.excerpt: The Lectric XP series has become something of an institution in the American electric bicycle market. As the country’s best-selling e-bike lineup, it’s helped put hundreds of thousands of riders on tw…
articles.body: The Lectric XP series has become something of an institution in the American electric bicycle market. As the country’s best-selling e-bike lineup, it’s helped put hundreds of thousands of riders on two wheels, largely thanks to its combination of affordable pricing, impressive performance, and practical features. It’s become the go-to electric bike in the US, but that hasn’t made Lectric complacent. Instead, the company is continuing to innovate. Now, Lectric is giving its flagship XP4 a fresh makeover with three new limited-edition versions, each sporting a unique color and a new collection of accessories and upgrades designed for different types of riders, from urban assault roles to conquering your favorite off-road fishing spots. more…
